steps.title: Select Mortality Cases
steps.instruction: Identify cases of uterine neoplasm mortality from secondary databases of epidemiological surveillance sectors of the Departments of the Family Health Strategy Women’s Health Program using ICD-10 codes C53, C54, and C55 for female residents of Maringá, Brazil, between 2004 and 2014.

steps.title: Extract and Classify Variables
steps.instruction: Extract demographic and socioeconomic variables from death certificates and the IBGE (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics) Demographic Census.

substeps.instruction: Divide age groups into ten-year increments.
Classify marital status as 'with partners' (married) or 'without partners' (single, divorced, or widowed).
Categorize education level by years of study according to Law 5692/71, with primary education defined as up to 8 years of school.

steps.title: Calculate Mortality Coefficients
steps.instruction: Calculate the Mortality Coefficients (CM) for the primary cause of death.

substeps.instruction: Use the total deaths from uterine neoplasms as the numerator.
Use the total female population exposed to the risk multiplied by 100,000 as the denominator.
Perform specific CM calculations for each ten-year age group.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Process and analyze the collected data using software and statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Enter data into Excel 2010 for Windows spreadsheets.
Conduct descriptive analysis calculating mean, median, maximum and minimum values, standard deviation, and absolute and relative frequencies (percentage).
Use the Pearson chi-square test for inferential analysis to confirm or refute descriptive evidence.

steps.title: Analyze Mortality Trends
steps.instruction: Apply a polynomial regression model to analyze trends in mortality coefficients.

substeps.instruction: Set CM as the dependent variable (y) and years of schooling as the independent variable (x).
Transform the 'year' variable into a year-centered variable (x-2009).
Smooth the series using a three-point moving average.
Test linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomial regression models, selecting the first-order (linear) model based on the dispersion diagram.
